summary: Two things worked. (1) Halving TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE from 2^19 to 2^18 (grad_accum 2->1) at unchanged LRs: 0.987981 vs the 0.997333 baseline; a three-point sweep (2^17 0.996087, 2^18 0.987981, 2^19 0.997333) puts the optimum essentially exactly at 2^18, so that axis is exhausted. (2) Spending the freed budget on width at that batch: dim 512->640->768 improves almost linearly at about -0.0030 per +128 dim, giving my best 0.982021 at dim 768/depth 8/MLP 4x/device batch 128. What did not work: more gradient averaging (adam beta1 0.9 + muon momentum 0.98) cost +0.0034, and all LRs x1.3 cost +0.0013, which together rule out 'the small-batch win is really an effective-LR increase' - it is genuinely about getting 2x the optimizer steps. Pushing width to 896 (with MLP 3x) turned the curve over at 0.993004, only 928 steps. One methodological result worth carrying forward: the same nominal 2^18 batch run as device batch 64 x accum 2 instead of 128 x 1 costs ~0.010 bpb, so grad accumulation silently confounds architecture comparisons at this scale. Next I would run dim 768 with SHORT_WINDOW_DIV 4 (worth about -0.003 at dim 640) and then re-check the batch optimum at the wider model, where the critical batch size may have moved up.
